The Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882 targeted Chinese laborers, whose immigration was seen as endangering "the good order of certain localities."  
The key economic activity driving Chinese immigration to the United States in the decades before 1882 was **railroad construction**, especially the building of the First Transcontinental Railroad in the 1860s–1870s, which employed thousands of Chinese laborers.  
While gold mining initially attracted Chinese immigrants during the California Gold Rush starting in 1849, railroad construction created a larger, more systematic demand for labor in the period just before the Act.
